about: The XCOM-style mode of the tactical game (T84): its shot, its cover and its pieces.

A piece's turn is two actions. Its type's movement is twice `action`: a walk that keeps the whole walk this turn within one action leaves it able to shoot; walking further is a dash, and spends it; a shot spends it.
Hit chance = shooter's aim - target's defence - cover, clamped to [0, 100]. One die per shot, from `die`; the shot hits when the die is below the chance, and a hit takes `damage` off the target.

Cover is read from the terrain beside the target: `full` next to rock, `half` next to trees. A cell of cover protects against a shooter on its side of the target; a shooter on no protected side has flanked it, and the target gets no cover.
Trees and rock block sight, except a cell beside either end of the line: a piece shoots past its own cover and at a target behind its.
A shot needs the target within `range` steps and in sight; a piece sees an enemy within its `sight` steps and in sight.
Aim, defence, damage, health, action, range and sight are this kit's numbers. Only `cover` and the two-action turn are borrowed (UFOpaedia, EU2012).

`search` is T87's Monte Carlo tree search: a playout stops after `playout_limit` answers and is scored on health; the enemy searches `iterations` a decision, `iterations_per_frame` of them each frame in the scene. `exploration` is UCB1's constant.
